#### correlation-null
*Variants:* correlation-null fields.
- **Meaning.** Vanishing in every separated correlation. The correlation-null elements of `V_d` form `N_d(S) = ∩_{v,f} ker L_{v,f}`, and `F_d = V_d / N_d(S)` (13:125–132: "equivalent to vanishing in every pointwise separated correlation"); "These functionals separate `F_d`, by the definition of correlation-null fields" (18:40).
  *Basis:* R (3:216, 523); D for the space (13:125–132). *Where:* 3:216, 523; 13:125–132; 18:40; 19:68. *Proposed:* *in the common kernel of the correlation functionals*; *fields all of whose separated correlations vanish*.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 3, 13, 18, 19. Chapters 18–19 use the term without recalling the definition of 13:125–132.
*See also:* correlation responses.

#### correlation responses
- **Meaning.** The one-slot responses: "For `c ∈ V_d`, a fixed spectator list `v`, and a separated smooth test function `f`, define the one-slot response `L_{v,f}(c) = ∫ f(x_0, x) S_{n+1}(c(x_0), v(x))`" (13:119–122).
  *Basis:* R (13:119–122). *Where:* 18:182; RG:18. *Proposed:* *the correlation functionals `L_{v,f}`*.
*Across chapters:* used in chapter 18 and the reading guide, defined in chapter 13. Not *correlations with all other fields* or *value of the functional*: *correlation functional* is kept because the object is the functional `c ↦ L_{v,f}(c)`, not a single value.
*See also:* correlation-null; one-slot response; spectators.

#### cost
*Variants:* costs (noun and verb); costing; minimum cost; replication costs; per-site normalization cost; positive action cost.
1. **A factor contributed to a bound**, usually a loss but also a gain: "costs `O(μ⁴)`" (7:618, a small factor) beside "costs `L⁴`" (7:619, a large one); as a noun, a polynomial loss (9:267, 434, 438, 712; 9s:273).
   *Basis:* R (7:618–619). *Where:* 4:378; 5:611, 620, 1354; ch. 6 (18 uses); ch. 7 (20), e.g. 7:359, 618–619, 674, 749–751, 905–910, 1120, 1126, 1175, 1178; 9:510, 610; ch. 10–11, e.g. 10:63, 166, 172, 178, 575, 601, 645; 11:197, 241, 432, 596, 925, 939, 1069; 11R:225, 254, 340; 13:237; 14:500, 589; 14lc:82; 18lp:41, 64, 85, 110, 113, 119, 178, 210, 212; ch. 17–19 (24 uses, listed with sense 3). *Proposed:* *contributes the factor …*; *loses a factor*; print the inequality.
2. **An additive term in an exponent or a logarithm**: "costs at least `Δ` in the exponent" (9s:147).
   *Basis:* R (9s:147). *Where:* 9s:147, 153, 160; 13sb:37; 14:757; 15sp:23; 18lp:107. *Proposed:* *adds … to the exponent*.
3. **The bound, or the error term, itself, as a named quantity**: "coefficient plus remainder cost at most `w`" (11:910); "additive value cost"; "per-site normalization cost `q^site`" (13sb:25, 112; 18lp:163); "normalized cost at most `ζ_h`" (13ba:120); "cost `q_fin`" (18lp:56); "Signed regular costs" (13sb:35); "absolute action cost per site" (11:789); an error term (14:199; 18lp:343).
   *Basis:* R (11:910; 13sb:25). *Where:* as quoted; in ch. 17–19 the 24 uses (17t:105, 108, 110, 163, 478; 17c:119, 364; 17w:59, 73, 108, 115; 17m:45, 130, 172, 180, 261, 301, 427, 428, 434; 18:230, 256; 18r:33; RG:26) are of senses 1–3 and were not split. *Proposed:* *bound*; *is bounded by*; name the quantity.
4. **The value of a function to be minimised**: "the minimum cost" is the minimum of the objective `P_e(u)` (4:391); "minimum-cost test" (5:967).
   *Basis:* R (4:391). *Where:* 4:391; 5:967. *Proposed:* *objective*; *value of `P_e`*.
5. **A lower bound on the action, or the small probability it yields**: "probability cost of a large-field region" (2:392); "a positive action cost is retained" (RG:26).
   *Basis:* I (2:392; RG:26). *Where:* 2:392; RG:26. *Proposed:* *a lower bound on the action*; *small probability*.
*Across chapters:* the same accounting word in every part of the book (18 uses in chapter 6; 32 in chapters 2, 7, 9; 10 / 22 / 10 in files 10, 11, 11R; 25 in chapters 12–16; 24 in chapters 17–19), with senses 1–3 everywhere and senses 4 and 5 isolated. Because sense 1 is used for gains as well as losses, *contributes a factor* is the safe equivalent. At 9:712 "all polynomial logarithmic costs" are factors polynomial in the logarithm, dominated by `(M_{m+1}^cut)²` (sense 1; text read). The `q_r` of 12:247 ("vacuum normalization bound"), the `q^site` of 13sb:24–25 and the `q` of (ch11:replicated-bound), defined at 11:810–811, are one quantity by the form of the bounds (inferred). Related accounting words in chapters 1, 2, 7–9: `gain` 9, `loss` 6, `reserve` 4, `share` 4, `spent` 1, `allocate` 1, `unused` 2.

#### counting coordinates
See *counting norm*.

#### counting norm
*Variants:* counting scalar product; counting adjoint; counting coordinates (11:621); physical counting norms (6:957).
- **Meaning.** The unnormalised `ℓ²` norm, scalar product and adjoint: sums over sites "without division by volume" (6:504).
  *Basis:* R (5:30, 40; 6:504). *Where:* 5:40, 528; 6:504, 957; 11:621. *Proposed:* *unnormalised `ℓ²` norm (scalar product, adjoint)*.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 5, 6. "Counting coordinates" (11:621) is read as the same convention (inferred). The "normalized counting measure" of 7:618, 644 is the normalised version and is not this term.

#### coupling band
*Variants:* (admissible) inverse coupling band; actual coupling band; `𝔅_m`.
- **Meaning.** The interval `𝔅_m = [β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]` in which the coupling `β` may lie at level `m`, around the reference value `β̂_m`: "The actual coupling ranges in `𝔅_m = [β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`" (4:418–419); "The admissible inverse coupling band at level `m` is `[β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`" (10:212).
  *Basis:* D (4:418–419; again 10:212). *Where:* 4:418–419; 6:623, 878; 9:386, 429, 949; 10:212; 17m:312. *Proposed:* *the interval `[β̂_m/2, 2β̂_m]`*; or keep, defined once.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. The definition is at 4:418–419 and is repeated at 10:212 (text read), so chapter 6 uses a term of chapter 4.
*See also:* coupling threshold.

#### coupling entry threshold
See *coupling threshold*.

#### coupling threshold
*Variants:* coupling thresholds; inverse coupling threshold (chapters 10–11); stage threshold `d_j` (10:157–158); coupling entry threshold (7:1190); coupling-threshold-controlled (17w:76); "the threshold" unqualified (9:202; 9s:219).
- **Meaning.** A lower bound imposed on the reference coupling `β̂` (at a stage, after the block ratio `L` has been chosen) above which the estimates hold: "choose `L` so that `C L^{-2} ≤ 1/4`, then the coupling entry threshold" (7:1189–1190); "Only afterwards choose inverse coupling thresholds and minimum auxiliary periods. Enlarging an inverse coupling threshold does not change the block ratio" (10:38–39); "Every subsequent stage threshold `d_j` is satisfied by increasing its starting scale until `β̂_m ≥ d_j`" (10:157–159); "sufficiently large coupling thresholds".
  *Basis:* R (7:1189–1190; 10:38–39, 157–158; 11:443–444). *Where:* 6:322, 432; 7:1190; 9:145, 430, 709; 9s:207; 10:38, 39, 110, 157–158 ("stage threshold `d_j`"), 627, 643; 11:278, 443, 711; 11E:32; 11R:10; 13:237; 13sb:16, 41, 45; 13ba:39, 50, 83, 101, 258, 261; 14lc:69; 18lp:101, 148; 17:134; 17w:23, 42, 74, 76, 95; 17c:141, 234, 236, 384, 386; 17m:142–143, 174, 185, 315, 346–347, 365, 430; 19:20 (19 uses in ch. 17–19). *Proposed:* *lower bound on `β̂`* (depending on the stage `j` and on `L`); in running text *for `β̂` sufficiently large*.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout; the parts agree, with two wordings of the same equivalent. "Threshold" alone is not safe: it is also the small-field threshold `t` (an upper bound on the field; 2:326; 9:19; 17c:316; 17m:304), a lower bound on the period (2e:210), a lower bound `N_0` on the cutoff (12:265; 13:27, 388), the "threshold for the starting scale" (10:63, 606, 692; 12:123), the mesh threshold (11:1119, 1815) and the restarted large-field threshold `ϑ` (11:749).
*See also:* coupling band.

#### cover
*Variants:* covering lattice; cover coefficients; cover row; cover paths; lift to the covering lattice.
1. **The infinite lattice `ℤ⁴` as universal cover of the tori**; "cover coefficients" and "cover row" are the kernel on `ℤ⁴`, as opposed to its periodisation.
   *Basis:* R (4:18; 5:735, 751). *Where:* 1:181; 2:291–295, 366, 381; 2e:210; 4:18; 5:735, 751, 806–849; 10:81; 11:399–400, 414. *Proposed:* *the infinite lattice `ℤ⁴`*; *infinite-volume kernel*.
2. **A connected cover of a set by balls of radius `B`**, in "connected cover number", "cover units", "fine cover number": see *connected covering number*.
   *Basis:* D (4:587–589). *Where:* 6:1296; 11:495, 1368. *Proposed:* as under *connected covering number*.
*Across chapters:* two ordinary senses that are easy to confuse in chapter 11, where both occur (11:399–414 against 11:495). "Fixed cover paths" (10:81) is assigned to sense 1 by inference only. A third use, "exact cover / coverage" (11:134–136), is the covering condition of an *exact cover*.

#### cover units
See *connected covering number* and *unit* (sense 3): "Retain two cover units beyond those needed by the connected expansion" (11:495).

#### coverage
See *exact cover*: the covering condition of an exact cover (11:134–136, 150, 180, 246–251; 11R:8, 124, 157, 167–168); also listed beside the exclusion support `Y_i` (4:440, 455–464).

#### covering number
See *connected covering number*.

#### crop
*Variants:* cropping; crop radius; crop tail.
- **Meaning.** Restriction of the coarse field to the ball of radius `C_j (log β̂_k)²`; the "crop tail" is what is discarded.
  *Basis:* R (17m:258). *Where:* 17m:258, 279, 289, 310, 313. *Proposed:* *truncation to a ball*.
*Across chapters:* 17m only; the word occurs in no other part of the book.

#### cross-modes
*Variants:* pushed spectator cross-modes.
- **Meaning.** The coefficients of the joint marked expansion that are indexed by sets of marks containing the score source together with one or more spectator marks, the spectators having been integrated down ("pushed") to the current level. "The same score source is used for every `A`, so the joint rooted expansion retains all pushed spectator cross-modes and this exact zero-moment statement" (17m:400–402). A "mode" is the coefficient of `z_I` for a subset `I` of marks.
  *Basis:* S for "mode"; I for "cross" and "pushed" (17m:393–402). *Where:* 17m:401. *Proposed:* *all mixed source–spectator coefficients*.
  *Source:* the coefficients are those of the monomials `z_I`, `I` a set of marks: Scott `part2/E-several-mark.tex:22` "Rescaling mark `h` by `𝗐_h > 0`, its mark weight, multiplies the coefficient of `z_I` by `∏_{h∈I} 𝗐_h`"; `part2/E-Gaussian-sources.tex:159` "to any mode in one cell" (the word "mode" for such a coefficient). `audit/ch17-score-independent-review.md:8, 45`: "All generated joint modes must remain …"; "retaining all original fine spectator modes". No Scott sentence has "cross-modes".
*Across chapters:* one occurrence.
*See also:* mode; spectators.

#### crude and grid constants
*Variants:* crude exponent; grid exponent.
- **Meaning.** The constants in the two estimates of the proof of the mixed bound in `18-lattice-products.tex`: the "crude" estimate with exponent `W + 1` ("give a crude exponent `W+1`: choose total excess one", 18lp:332–334) and the estimate on grid configurations with exponent `θ_+ W + c_1` ("The grid exponent is `θ_+W + c_1`", 18lp:335–337). "The crude and grid constants are uniform in the character" (18r:51).
  *Basis:* R (18lp:332–341). *Where:* 18r:51; 18lp:332–341. *Proposed:* *the constants of the two estimates (crude, on the grid) in the proof of Proposition 18.mixed-bound*; cite them.
*Across chapters:* used in 18r, determined in 18lp. Text read at 18lp:320–341.

#### cubic momentum functional
See *coefficient functional*.

#### curl-division
*Variants:* curl division (17c:346); two-leg division (7:1162).
- **Meaning.** The division by the lattice curl of chapter 7 (section "Division by the lattice curl", 7:67 ff.), built from the elementary division `D_a f(p) = (f(p) − f(p|_{p_a=0}))/(e^{ip_a} − 1)` (7:89–91). Chapter 10 fixes these linear operations once in order to make the representation by transported curvature terms unique (10:313–316).
  *Basis:* R (7:67, 89–91; 10:313–316). *Where:* 10:314; 17c:346 (unhyphenated: "Two-leg curl division leaves one extra difference"); 7:1162 ("the two-leg division"). *Proposed:* *division by the lattice curl (Section 7.…)*; keep, cite chapter 7.
*Across chapters:* defined in chapter 7, used in chapters 10 and 17c (text read at 10:313–316 and 7:67, 88–91). The "path-placement operations" fixed in the same sentence (10:314–315) were not found under that name in chapter 7 (7:753 has "placement" in another sense); their meaning stays open (`?`).

#### current defect
*Variants:* current defect `𝓔_b`.
- **Meaning.** `𝓔_b = Σ_a ∇_a J_ab − D𝖲[Y_b]`: the failure of the lattice Ward identity, that is, of conservation of the current up to the equation-of-motion term.
  *Basis:* D (17:194–195). *Where:* 17:194, 244; 17t:157, 408, 416; 17c:6, 13, 17 and 12 more; 17m:154 (21 uses in prose). *Proposed:* *defect of the lattice Ward identity*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only; a new sense of "defect" relative to the *curvature defect* of chapters 5–6. The TeX comment line 17c:2 is not counted.
*See also:* curvature defect.

#### current depth
- **Meaning.** The number of block transformations applied to the current ("Choose the current depth and then the period at each fixed `k`", 17m:361; "a deep transferred current", 17m:29).
  *Basis:* I (17m:29, 361). *Where:* 17m:29, 361. *Proposed:* *number of steps*.
*Across chapters:* 17m only. Whether the depth of 17m:361 is a further limit inside the ordered limit of 13:44–50 is not determined.

#### curvature coordinate
- **Meaning.** The scalar function `U ↦ ⟨u, σ_{γ,□}(U)⟩`, a component of the transported plaquette curvature paired with `u ∈ 𝔤`. The subsection title (2e:60) calls these "curvature tests".
  *Basis:* D (2e:62–67). *Where:* 2e:60, 65–68, 104, 124, 172, 184, 194. *Proposed:* keep, define once; drop "tests" in the title.
*Across chapters:* 2e only.
*See also:* curvature insertion; curvature measurement.

#### curvature defect
*Variants:* defect (chapters 5–6); amended curvature defect (5:1371).
- **Meaning.** `Z₀ = B_c − T* B_f T − b⁻¹ d_{1,c} d_{1,c}*` with `B = H⁻¹` for the unmodified metrics (5:638–641). The "amended curvature defect" (5:1371) is the same expression with the modified inverse metrics `B̃_c`, `B̃_f` (5:662–666, 674–676), which is positive: `H̃_c (B̃_c − T* B̃_f T − b⁻¹ d_{1,c} d_{1,c}*) H̃_c = d_{2,c}* D_c* R₀ D_c d_{2,c}` (5:672–680), and in chapter 6 `K*K = 𝖡_c − T* 𝖡_f T − b⁻¹ d_{1,c} d_{1,c}*` (6:147–148; the text has no symbol for this modified quantity).
  *Basis:* R (5:638–641, 672–680; 6:147–148). *Where:* 5:453 (title), 603, 638–641, 672–680, 1371; 6:135, 145–148. *Proposed:* *positive remainder in the recursion for `H⁻¹`* (no standard name known).
*Across chapters:* chapters 5–6. The compound "curvature defect" itself occurs only at 5:453 and 5:1371; 5:603 and 6:135 have "defect" and "positive-defect". At 6:213 "the two signed defects" are instead `E_L`, `E_D`; in chapter 17 "defect" is the *current defect*, and at 14:932–937 there is a space of "internal defects". At 6:176 the word is only in a label.
*See also:* current defect; curvature metric.

#### curvature family
*Variants:* cubic, quartic, quadratic curvature family.
- **Meaning.** A family of transported curvature terms representing a homogeneous part of an action. The cubic and quartic families are (inferred) the "invariant cubic and quartic curvature terms `S_3`, `S_4`" of Proposition "Classical matching" (7:994–997): "the cubic and quartic curvature families are constructed" (7:1071); "the cubic/quartic families of Proposition (ch07:classical-match)" (7:1168–1169). The lines 7:1060–1062 ("the quartic contribution of the constructed cubic family … linear in that cubic family") name no symbol. The quadratic family of 7:1163, produced by "Lemma (ch07:unique) and the two-leg division" (7:1162), is a separate object without a symbol.
  *Basis:* I (7:994–997 with 7:1071, 1168–1169). *Where:* 7:1054, 1060–1062, 1071, 1163, 1168. *Proposed:* *the terms `S_3`, `S_4`*; *the quadratic curvature terms* for 7:1163.
*Across chapters:* chapter 7 only.

#### curvature insertion
*Variants:* curvature insertion `F_{γ,ab}`.
- **Meaning.** The transported projected plaquette curvature `F_{γ,ab}`; the same object as the "transported curvature" `σ_{γ,□}` of chapter 2 (2:171–175).
  *Basis:* D (7:147–152). *Where:* 7:147–152. *Proposed:* *transported curvature* (one name for chapters 2 and 7).
*Across chapters:* chapter 7; the object is that of chapter 2 under another name.
*See also:* curvature coordinate; curvature measurement.

#### curvature measurement
- **Meaning.** The maps `J ↦ σ_{γ,□}(U(1,J))`, that is, the transported curvatures as functions of the jet, and their linearisations.
  *Basis:* I (2:220, 238). *Where:* 2:220, 238, 362. *Proposed:* *transported curvatures (as functions of the jet)*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 2 only. "Curvature measurement", "curvature coordinate" (with "curvature test") and "curvature insertion" are not synonyms: they are three related objects (a `𝔤`-valued function; its scalar components; the same function of the jet).
*See also:* curvature coordinate; curvature insertion.

#### curvature metric
*Variants:* two-form metric; metric (chapters 5–7).
- **Meaning.** A positive operator `H` on two-forms, with `K = d₁* H d₁` the operator of the quadratic action `S₀(a) = ½⟨d₁a, H d₁a⟩`.
  *Basis:* D (5:43–46). *Where:* 5:43–46, 227–235, 286–291, 456; 6:139, 163; 7:312, 974. *Proposed:* *quadratic form on two-forms*; *coefficient operator `H`*.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 5–7.
*See also:* completion; curvature defect.

#### cutoff
*Variants:* ultraviolet cutoff; outer cutoff; terminal cutoff; smooth cutoff; cutoff function; level-`m` cutoff; cutoff threshold; cutoff tail; cutoff condition; cutoff-to-noise ratio.
1. **The ultraviolet cutoff `N`** (the finest level). "Outer cutoff" is `N` (13ba:53, 221); "cutoff threshold" is the `N_0` beyond which a bound holds (12:265; 13:27, 388); "cutoff tail" means all sufficiently large `N` (12:190, 249; 13sb:84).
   *Basis:* R (5:705–706). *Where:* 1:15, 209, 387; 5:705; 9:947; ch. 10 passim; most of the 66 uses in ch. 12–16. *Proposed:* *ultraviolet cutoff `N`*; *for all sufficiently large `N`*.
2. **A smooth cutoff function** (`χ` in chapters 3, 14, 16; `γ` in chapter 11).
   *Basis:* R (3:758; 11:544–557). *Where:* 3:758; 9:476; 11:314, 544–557, 708; 13ba:36, 68, 165; 14:252, 324, 328, 347, 396, 614, 620, 625, 736; 16:205, 232, 235, 283, 459, 539. *Proposed:* *cutoff function*.
3. **A threshold on the field, or the indicator of the condition it defines**: `ε_pred`, `t_m` (4:203, 211, 406); "level-`m` cutoff" (12:187); "pass the cutoff" (9s:126–127); "cutoff-to-noise ratio" (11R:61).
   *Basis:* R (4:203, 406). *Where:* 4:203, 211, 406; 7:25; 9:111, 840; 9s:10, 127; 11R:61; 12:187. *Proposed:* *threshold*; *small-field condition*.
4. **Truncation of the path length at `R_*`**.
   *Basis:* R (6:23). *Where:* 6:23, 905; 11:672. *Proposed:* *path-length truncation*.
*Across chapters:* all four senses run through the book. At 14:324 "independent of the cutoff" refers to the function `χ`, not to `N`. The compounds "cutoff failure", "failed cutoff condition" have their own entry; they are not *large-field events*. "Cutoff tail" (12:190, 249; 13sb:84) is not the *ordered tail*.
*See also:* cutoff amplitude; cutoff failure; cutoff remainder.

#### cutoff amplitude
*Variants:* `M = M^cut`; `M_m^cut`.
- **Meaning.** `M_m^cut = exp((log log β̂_m)²)`, the ratio that fixes the small-field threshold `t_m = β̂_m^{-1/2} M_m^cut`.
  *Basis:* D (4:410–413). *Where:* 4:410–413; 9:137 and passim; 9s:23; 17:104. *Proposed:* *threshold ratio* (unsure; nothing better found); keep the symbol.
*Across chapters:* one object; chapters 9 and 17 use the chapter 4 symbol without recalling it, and the same formula appears as `H_k` at 14lc:23–24 and as `M_n`, `H_n`, `H` in chapter 17.
*See also:* cutoff (sense 3).

#### cutoff failure
*Variants:* failed cutoff condition; failed-cutoff factor; failed remote cutoff (9:280); cutoff-failure indicator, label, probability, catalogue; failures of smooth local cutoffs.
1. **The event that a Gaussian coordinate is large where the field is small**, so that a smooth local cutoff differs from one: "Failures of smooth local cutoffs in the remaining coordinates are controlled by simultaneous Gaussian tail estimates" (6:9–10); the event is `ℰ_w = {∃ i : d(i,w) ≤ 2B, |z_i| ≥ T}`, `T = ξ t_f/(2g)` (6:837–843). In chapter 9: "Distinct cutoff-failure labels" (9:111); "cutoff failure at a distinct label" (9:133); "a failed remote cutoff has the joint Gaussian-tail bound of Chapter 6" (9:280).
   *Basis:* R (6:7–11, 837–843). *Where:* 6:9, 1018; 9:111, 133, 280; 10:532, 595–597, 727; 11:1613; 11R:283–284, 311. *Proposed:* *cutoff-failure event* (defined once); *the event `{|z_i| ≥ T for some i near w}`*. Not *large-field event*.
2. **Failure of the small-field indicator, that is, presence of a large-field site**: "a complementary stencil containing a failed cutoff condition meets at least one selected support" (11:150–151); the "failed-cutoff factor" `1 − (1−χ) R z_I`, whose "support contains a large-field indicator covered by an original prescribed large-field set" (11:1487–1497); "Every nonzero failed cutoff and every old large-field activity meets a new large-field site" (11:1932–1933).
   *Basis:* R (11:150–151, 1487–1497). *Where:* 11:150–151, 1476–1500, 1523, 1562, 1932–1933; 11R:378. *Proposed:* *failure of the small-field indicator*; *large-field site*.
*Across chapters:* Not *large-field event* for sense 1: chapter 6 separates the two mechanisms (6:7–11). Text read (6:1014–1019; 10:530–533; 11:147–152, 1486–1492, 1611–1614, 1931–1934): chapters 6, 9, 10 and part of chapter 11 have sense 1, and chapter 11 also has sense 2. The "cutoff-failure catalogue" (10:727, once; undefined) is read as the list of these events, part of the combinatorial data fixed at each level independently of `N` (inferred); with the clipping data, *the fixed data: prescribed large-field sets, list of cutoff events, clip parameters*. 10:393 ("event indicators") and 10:921 ("clipping data") name the same fixed data without the word. "Tail events" (11R:43–45, 283–284) are the events of sense 1, those of (ch06:tail-event). "Warnings" (6:1476; 11:319) probably refers to sense 1; inferred.
*See also:* complementary; cutoff-failure label; cutoff remainder.

#### cutoff-failure catalogue
See *cutoff failure*.

#### cutoff-failure event
See *cutoff failure* (sense 1). This is the one word chosen for the event that a Gaussian coordinate is large where the field is small, `ℰ_w = {∃ i : d(i,w) ≤ 2B, |z_i| ≥ T}` (6:837–843), so that a smooth local cutoff differs from one; never *large-field event* (6:7–11). The phrase itself does not occur in the chapters; the text has "failures of smooth local cutoffs" (6:9), "cutoff-failure indicator" (6:1018), "tail events" (6:1137; 11R:43) and "large-coordinate event" (6:835).

#### cutoff-failure label
- **Meaning.** The event label `w` of chapter 6 (6:835–837), which indexes the events of *cutoff failure* (sense 1).
  *Basis:* I (9:111). *Where:* 9:111, 133. *Proposed:* *event label* (one name for chapters 6 and 9).
*Across chapters:* chapter 6 says "event label", chapter 9 "cutoff-failure label"; chapters 10–11 say "event indicator" and do not use either.

#### cutoff remainder
- **Meaning.** The object bounded in the tail estimates of chapter 6: "A cutoff remainder is bounded but need not be pointwise small. Its smallness comes from a large-coordinate event" (6:834–835); a remainder with event label `w` vanishes unless `ℰ_w` occurs (6:837–843). The remainder itself is not defined; that it is the difference produced by a smooth cutoff being different from one is inferred.
  *Basis:* R (6:834–843) for its properties; I for what it is. *Where:* 6:739, 834–843, 892–897, 1018, 1040. *Proposed:* keep *cutoff remainder*, once defined.
*Across chapters:* chapter 6 only. These Gaussian-tail objects are distinct from the large-field selection `A` and from `Bad_m(U)`, which the chapter treats by a separate mechanism (6:7–11).
*See also:* cutoff failure.

#### cutoff tail
See *cutoff* (sense 1). Not the *ordered tail*.

### D

#### damping
*Variants:* heat damping; undamped measure; damped moment.
- **Meaning.** The factor `e^{−2uE}` produced in the spectral representation when the insertion is translated to time `u > 0`; the undamped measure is the spectral measure with this factor removed.
  *Basis:* D for "undamped measure" (14:416–419); R for the rest. *Where:* 14:416, 430, 435, 436, 489, 513, 752, 765. *Proposed:* *the weight `e^{−2uE}`*; *spectral measure with the factor `e^{2uE}` restored*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 14 only.
*See also:* heat; annular correction.

#### declared
*Variants:* declaration.
- **Meaning.** Program vocabulary. "Declared" stands for "stated" (of hypotheses and results: 3:441; 4:20) or for "classified as" ("sites declared to be in the large-field region", 8:284; "never declared large-field", 11:441); "A declaration that exponents lie in `[98,100]`" (11:534) is an assumption.
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 3:441; 4:20, 505, 626, 674; 6:1343, 1543 (the line list covers the whole group declared, inputs, export, reachable, stored); 8:284; 11:441, 534. *Proposed:* *stated*; *classified as*; *assumed*.
*Across chapters:* one register throughout, three ordinary meanings.
*See also:* stored; reachable.

#### deep transferred current
- **Meaning.** A current to which many block transformations have been applied: "not the uncontrolled higher derivatives of a deep transferred current" (17m:29).
  *Basis:* I (17m:29). *Where:* 17m:29. *Proposed:* *current transferred through many steps*; for the depth, *number of steps*.
*Across chapters:* single occurrence.
*See also:* current depth; transfer.

#### defect
*Variants:* defects; signed defects; quadratic defect; defect Ward identity.
1. **Place where the small-curvature condition fails.** "Connected sets of defects are summed" (1:457).
   *Basis:* I (1:457). *Where:* 1:457. *Proposed:* *large-field regions* (or *large-field sites*).
2. **Curvature defect** `Z₀ = B_c − T*B_fT − b⁻¹d₁d₁*`; "the two signed defects" of 6:213 are `E_L`, `E_D`.
   *Basis:* R (5:638–641). *Where:* 5:638–641; 6:135, 213. *Proposed:* as for *curvature defect*; write the symbols.
3. **Current defect** `𝓔_b = Σ_a ∇_a J_ab − D𝖲[Y_b]`: the failure of the lattice Ward identity, that is, of current conservation up to the equation-of-motion term. "The removed gradient is killed by the defect Ward identity" (17c:66) refers to an identity for this defect; the line does not say which.
   *Basis:* D (17:194–195). *Where:* 17:194, 244; 17t:157, 408, 416; 17c:6, 13, 17 and 12 more; 17m:154 (21 uses in prose). *Proposed:* *defect of the lattice Ward identity*.
4. **Internal defect** `[L(K), L(M)] − L([K, M])`, the failure of the rotation generators to represent the Lie bracket.
   *Basis:* R (14:931–933). *Where:* 3:910; 14:932–937. *Proposed:* as for *internal rotation defect*.
*Across chapters:* four objects under one word: sense 1 once, in the introduction; sense 2 in chapters 5–6; sense 4 in chapters 3 and 14; sense 3 in chapter 17, where it is new relative to the curvature defect.
*See also:* `Bad_m(U)`; curvature defect; current defect; defect space; internal defect.

#### defect space
- **Meaning.** The space in which the internal defect `[L(K), L(M)] − L([K, M])` lies: "The finite internal-defect correlation functionals … are injective on this defect space" (14:936–937). The space is not written down.
  *Basis:* I (14:932–937). *Where:* 14:937. *Proposed:* state the object each time (*the space of maps with the properties listed at 14:933–935*).
*Across chapters:* single occurrence.
*See also:* defect (sense 4).

#### defect Ward identity
See *defect* (sense 3).

#### degree
1. **Scaling dimension of a label:** the filtration degree `d` of `V_d`, `F_d`; 18gq:19 warns "scaling dimension …, not its factor count".
   *Basis:* R (18gq:19). *Where:* ch. 12–16 passim. *Proposed:* *scaling dimension `d`*.
2. **Number of field factors** (Taylor degree).
   *Basis:* R (7:1079). *Where:* 7:1079. *Proposed:* *order in the field*.
3. **Number of elementary factors** of an elementary factor, polymer or cluster.
   *Basis:* D (9:172–174). *Where:* 9:172–174, 182, 193. *Proposed:* *number of elementary factors*.
4. **Degree in the curvature** of an elementary term of the path action ("atom of degree `q`").
   *Basis:* I (5:1054–1056). *Where:* 5:1054–1056; 11R:137; 12:60. *Proposed:* *degree `q` in the curvature*.
5. **Ordinary uses:** polynomial degree; "source degree" (12:270; number of source variables); "radial degree" (18lp:173); "degree of the Killing field" (14:347); "spatial momentum degree, not the field degree" (17c:17–23).
   *Basis:* R. *Where:* as listed. *Proposed:* keep, with the qualifier.
*Across chapters:* the word changes meaning with the object it grades; chapters 9 and 18gq each say which count is meant, the others rely on context.
*See also:* arity; atom; bidegree; degree ceiling; degree menu; factor count.

#### degree ceiling
- **Meaning.** The maximal degree, fixed before the schedule: "Fix the degree ceiling before the schedule" (13ba:56).
  *Basis:* I (13ba:56). *Where:* 13ba:56. *Proposed:* *maximal degree*.
*Across chapters:* single occurrence.
*See also:* degree; schedule.

#### degree-`d` section
See *section*.

#### degree menu
*Variants:* menu (of stencil radii and degrees).
- **Meaning.** A finite list of degrees.
  *Basis:* R (11:161, 516). *Where:* 11:161, 516. *Proposed:* *finite list*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only.
*See also:* degree; menu.

#### delay
*Variants:* stage delay; finite delays; uniform delay; terminal delays (10:107–112).
- **Meaning.** The requirement that a stage, or the cutoff level, start at a sufficiently large level `m`, so that a fixed constant is dominated by a slowly growing quantity or an inverse-coupling threshold is met: "Every subsequent stage threshold `d_j` is satisfied by increasing its starting scale until `β̂_m ≥ d_j`" (10:157–159); "The stage delay can impose `C_k ≤ H^γ`" (11:1192); "The stage choices of sufficiently large starting scales impose a common bound `H^{ε_j}` … This uniform delay" (11:1397–1402). The delays of 10:107–112 are the same kind of condition at the cutoff level `N`: "absorbed by choosing sufficiently large inverse-coupling thresholds", they "also impose `β̂_N ≥ a_{d,J(N)}`", which 11E:29–30 places "in the adjacent stage conditions on the starting scale".
  *Basis:* R (10:157–159; 11:1397–1402; 10:107–112). *Where:* 10:107, 111; 11:1192, 1199, 1214, 1267, 1270, 1402, 1764, 1944, 2022, 2085, 2111, 2146. *Proposed:* *lower bound on the starting level of the stage*; state the inequality imposed (`β̂_m ≥ d_j`, `β̂_N ≥ a_{d,J(N)}`).
*Across chapters:* chapters 10–11 only; one kind of condition, the terminal delays of 10:107–112 included. The same condition is also written "threshold for the starting scale", "condition on the starting scale", "stage entrance".
*See also:* stage; coupling threshold; block floor.

#### deletion-of-support identities
- **Meaning.** Probably the identity (ch08:deletion-identity): "delete all labels whose supports meet `Y`", `Z_pol(z^Y)/Z_pol(z) = e^{−𝓛_Y(z)}` (8:208–215). Inferred from the name and from the reference to chapter 8 at 11R:367.
  *Basis:* I (11R:239; 8:208–215). *Where:* 11R:239. *Proposed:* cite the identity (8:208–215).
*Across chapters:* single occurrence, pointing back to chapter 8.

#### denominator
*Variants:* zero-background denominator; vector / ghost / channel denominator; free quadratic denominator; vacuum denominator (12:286).
1. **The symbol `a(k)` of the zero-background operator,** a matrix, whose inverse is the propagator; `b`, `c` are its background insertions.
   *Basis:* R (7:331). *Where:* 7:331, 371, 376, 407, 414–415, 440; 17t:107 ("denominator floor"). *Proposed:* *symbol of the quadratic form*; *inverse propagator*.
2. **The normalising integral without insertions** (the integral of the density without sources, by which correlations are divided).
   *Basis:* I (12:286); R via chapter 11 (11:604, 773, 2101) for 17w:88 and 17m:418, where it is the integral of the empty density. *Where:* 12:286; 17w:88; 17m:418. *Proposed:* *the partition function* (*the normalization without insertions*).
*Across chapters:* two unrelated senses: chapter 7 (and 17t) against chapters 12 and 17.
*See also:* background insertion; empty coefficient; floor.

#### density coordinates
*Variants:* coordinate tuple; "the coordinates of Chapter 4" (9:6–7).
- **Meaning.** The data `(β, v_sc, regular activities, large-field activities)` that represent a density. The tuples satisfying the norm bounds form a "much larger set" than the reachable outputs (4:674–677), and a tuple "need not give a positive density" (4:567); the text says nothing on injectivity. That these are therefore not coordinates in the usual sense is an inference.
  *Basis:* D (4:550). *Where:* 4:8, 403, 469, 530, 550, 656–676; 9:6–7, 399, 717–720, 904. *Proposed:* *representation of the density* (*representation data `(β, v_sc, activities)`*).
*Across chapters:* one object; chapters 10–11 call it "local representation" and "presentation". Not *parametrisation*: nothing in the text makes the data a parametrisation. The phrase at 9:6–7 is "in the coordinates of Chapter 4".
*See also:* presentation; scalar.

#### density identity
- **Meaning.** The identity `div_Haar(F Y) = ∫ 𝒟_Y k f dU` for the block integral `F` with kernel `k` and a vector field `Y` (emphasised in the text).
  *Basis:* D (17m:63–66). *Where:* 17m:62–66. *Proposed:* keep, or *differentiated kernel identity*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only.
*See also:* density-valued insertion; displacement.

#### density-valued insertion
*Variants:* density-valued kernel insertion; score source; zero-moment source; full source.
- **Meaning.** The factor `𝒟_Y k`, the kernel differentiated along the vector field `Y`, inserted in the block integral in place of `k`.
  *Basis:* R (17m:68). *Where:* 17m:68, 155, 391, 400, 412, 443, 459. *Proposed:* *the differentiated kernel `𝒟_Y k`*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only; a use of "insertion" for a non-observable factor.
*See also:* density identity; marked; score; source.

#### derivative descent
See *descent* (sense 2).

#### derivative reserve
*Variants:* derivative reserves; one derivative reserve.
- **Meaning.** Derivative orders beyond the order of the output norm, kept for a later estimate: "through one order beyond the outgoing order. This is a numerical derivative reserve for the integration kernels" (10:737–739). That 9:34 ("with the prescribed derivative reserves for the local integral estimates") means the same is inferred.
  *Basis:* R (10:737–739); I (9:34; ch. 17). *Where:* 9:34; 10:738; 17w:84; 17m:49, 103, 198, 282 (the last list covers derivative, support and width reserves). *Proposed:* *additional derivative orders*; *one additional derivative*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; used in chapter 9 before chapter 10 explains it.
*See also:* reserve.

#### derivative-transport argument
- **Meaning.** The Proposition "Derivative transport and smooth comparison" (14:229–238): `r_k U_{k,d+1}^{-1} ∂_a U_{k,d} → ∂_a^0`, that is, conjugation of the derivative by the comparison maps.
  *Basis:* R (14:229–238). *Where:* 17:128. *Proposed:* cite the proposition by number.
*Across chapters:* a pointer from chapter 17 to chapter 14.
*See also:* transport.

#### descendants
- **Meaning.** Tree vocabulary for nested collision subsets, with "child" and "parent" operators: the operators attached to the subsets nested in a given one.
  *Basis:* I (18:404–418). *Where:* 18:404–418. *Proposed:* *operators of the nested subsets*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 18 only.
*See also:* child operators.

#### descending graph
See *descent* (sense 1).

#### descent
*Variants:* descend; descending induction; derivative descent; trial descent; bulk descent bound; descending graph; quantitative descent (7:1187).
1. **Transfer down the block steps** of a trial, a polynomial or a graph, from fine to coarse: the backward comparison of 11:890–917 ("Descend this whole polynomial to `m`", 13ba:170; "ordinary trial descent gives", 17m:461; "the descending graph", 17m:444). Not a downward induction (11:908–909).
   *Basis:* R (11:890–917). *Where:* 11:945, 2311; 11E:125, 148; 13:239; 13ba:170; 17m:444, 461, 469; the argument is named "backward comparison", not "descent", at 11:27, 890 and 11E:121 (only the label of the section 11:890 has "trial-descent"). *Proposed:* *transfer down the block steps*; for the named argument, *backward comparison* (cited by section number); "graph" is kept.
2. **Downward induction** on a degree, a layer or a level: "Descending through the degree" (2:236); "Descending through the layers" (2e:102); "Descending removes every jet order above `g`" (3:903); "descending from the highest nonzero homogeneous" (11:1821); "finite descending induction" (11R:386); "Descend in total degree" (18lp:342).
   *Basis:* R (18r:48, 53). *Where:* 2:236; 2e:102; 3:903; 11:1821; 11R:386; 18r:48, 53; 18lp:342. *Proposed:* *downward induction on the degree* (on the layer, on the level).
3. **Passage to a quotient** ("These maps descend to unique maps", 13:263; "The operators descend and extend to self-adjoint contractions", 14:51). Standard.
   *Basis:* R (13:263; 14:51). *Where:* 13:263, 274; 14:51; 16:135. *Proposed:* keep.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes: sense 1 in chapters 11, 13 and 17m; sense 2 in chapters 2, 3, 11, 11R and 18; sense 3 in chapters 13–16. For sense 1, *transfer* is the one verb for moving an object through the block steps (not *propagation*). "Quantitative descent" (7:1187), the step from the loop bound at `m+1` to that at `m`, is a fourth use (*induction step*). "Descend to level one" (10:271) is passage to a lower level (ordinary).
*See also:* backward comparison; transfer; trial.

#### detecting family
See *separating family*. One occurrence: "Free finite detecting families from Chapter 3" (14:221).

#### detection
*Variants:* detect; detecting families (14:221); rank detection (13sb:9); detector (labels only).
- **Meaning.** The property that a finite family of correlation functionals separates the elements of a quotient: `P ∉ N_D` if and only if some correlation with `P` is nonzero. The text's own words are "separates" and "separating family" (3:484, 775, 779, 806), which have replaced "detecting" in most places (13:14, 395; 14:386, 832; 15:17, 250, 256).
  *Basis:* I (3:830); the separating family is defined at 3:484, 806. *Where:* 3:830; 11:960 (title), 976; 11E:171; 13sb:9; 14:221. *Proposed:* *separating family*; *the family separates …*.
*Across chapters:* one sense. Not *nondegeneracy*: the text's own term, *separating family*, is used. "Separated" also means "at pairwise distinct points" (1:359; 3:104, 144–145), so "separation" cannot be reserved for this property. Detection is the property, not the value of a correlation functional.
*See also:* separating family; probe; measurement.

#### detector
See *detection*. The word occurs in labels only (`ch11:detectors`, `ch11:detector-bound`, `ch11:uniform-detector`, `ch11:finite-detector-input`, `ch11:simultaneous-detector-lifts`, `ch15:detector-moments`), not in the prose of any chapter.

#### determinant inverse identity
- **Meaning.** Probably the expansions of 6:1192–1203 ("The exact inverse and trace expansions … This determinant identity").
  *Basis:* I (9:140; 6:1192–1203). *Where:* 9:140. *Proposed:* replace by a reference to 6:1192–1203.
*Across chapters:* a pointer from chapter 9 to chapter 6.

#### determinant-word series
- **Meaning.** The series of Neumann-series terms ("words", in the sense of 6:1199 ff.) in the expansion of a determinant.
  *Basis:* R via chapter 6 (6:1199 ff.). *Where:* 11R:270. *Proposed:* *Neumann series of the determinant*; *terms of the series*.
*Across chapters:* single occurrence, using the chapter 6 sense of "word".
*See also:* word; determinant inverse identity.

#### deterministic coefficient evaluation
*Variants:* coefficient evaluation; coefficient recovery; coefficient conversions.
- **Meaning.** Evaluation of the extraction functional on polynomial inputs with the Gaussian fluctuation set to zero; "recovery" is the inversion of a finite matrix of pairings.
  *Basis:* I (17m:251–301). *Where:* 17m:251–301, 471. *Proposed:* *value of the coefficient functional at `gz = 0`*; *inversion of the finite system*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only; contrasted with the "actual conditional insertion" (17m:276–294).

#### diagonal
*Variants:* below the diagonal; diagonal factor; diagonal transfer.
- **Meaning.** In the triangular recursion (17c:216) for the norms `e_r`: the diagonal entry is the coefficient of `e_r` in `e′_r`, the terms below the diagonal those with `s < r`. "Its diagonal transfer is `C_j L⁴ L⁻⁵`" (17c:347) is that numerical factor.
  *Basis:* R (17c:216). *Where:* 17c:140, 211, 228, 235–237, 346, 367, 369, 375, 383. *Proposed:* *the coefficient `a_{j,r}(L)`*; *the terms with `s < r`*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17c. Other uses are standard: the diagonals of coincident points (1:365), diagonal subsequences (see *diagonalize*).
*See also:* diagonalize; row sum.

#### diagonalize
*Variants:* Diagonalize (… requests); diagonal radius selection (17m:446); diagonal extraction.
- **Meaning.** Take a diagonal subsequence over countably many finite requirements: "Diagonalize finite degree, arity, window and derivative requests" (17:139–140), parallel to 14:224–227 "A single sequence for all requests is obtained only by explicitly diagonalizing arity, degree, compact windows and errors".
  *Basis:* R via chapter 14 (14:224–227). *Where:* 17:139; 17m:446; 19:38, 112. *Proposed:* *take a diagonal subsequence over …*.
*Across chapters:* one sense; not diagonalisation of an operator.
*See also:* request; extraction.

#### dictionary
*Variants:* common dictionary; common coefficient dictionary; support dictionary; fixed dictionaries; dictionary of local supports and inventories (12:23).
- **Meaning.** The index set on which coefficient or activity families are defined, common to all cutoffs: "coefficients `c_N(γ)` on a common dictionary" (10:375–376). At 12:23–26 it carries more than indices: "use one dictionary of local supports and large-field inventories for all cutoffs `N > m`. All small-field event indicators and eligibility criteria in this dictionary are fixed at level `m`". No sentence says what a dictionary is.
  *Basis:* R / I (10:375–376; 12:23–26). *Where:* 10:316, 376, 379, 382, 393, 727, 905; 11:472; 12:23, 25. *Proposed:* *common index set* (*of paths*, *of supports*); at 12:23–26 *common list of supports and large-field sets, with their indicators*.
*Across chapters:* one sense in chapters 10–12; in chapter 12 the dictionary carries the indicators as well as the index set.
*See also:* array; inventory.

#### dimensionless directions
See *normalized directions*.

#### direct
*Variants:* direct row; direct term; direct row coefficient; `c_dir`.
- **Meaning.** The single-plaquette term of the action and its coefficient `c_dir`, as in `H = c_dir I + ρ*ρ` (7:974).
  *Basis:* I; the constant `c_dir` is fixed at 4:474–480. *Where:* 4:474; 5:749; 6:101, 137, 143 ff.; 7:352–354, 974–975; 9:36, 568, 752; 10:356; 11:752. *Proposed:* *plaquette term*; *its coefficient `c_dir`*.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout.
*See also:* row.

#### direction selectors
- **Meaning.** The four linear maps `J_a` (`a = 1,…,4`) from one-forms (link fields) to site fields, `(J_a u)(x) = u(x,a)`. The vector regulator is `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* m_μ J_a`, which is "`M_μ` applies `m_μ` to each one-form component" (7:276). They depend neither on the background field nor on the momentum, so they contribute nothing to the derivatives: "The four constant direction selectors in the vector regulator do not change these powers" (7:427–428).
  *Basis:* S; I from the v3 text (7:276, 427). *Where:* 7:427. *Proposed:* *the four constant maps `J_a` taking a one-form to its `a`-th component*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/C-section.tex:259`: "let `J_a` select direction `a` from fine links, so `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* 𝔪_μ J_a`"; `:348` "The constant direction selectors in the vector regulator preserve these bounds." Martin `existence/annulus-same-data-binding.tex:367–368`: "The direction selectors are constant matrices, so their marked slots are zero." Lean `YM.Stationary.copiesV`, `YM.Stationary.brigadeM`, `YM.Stationary.rankAux`, `YM/Next/STATIONARY/Spectral/AuxReferences.lean` (definitions read): `copiesV a` is the component map (lemma `notes_u`, statement read), `brigadeM U = Σ_a (J_a)ᵀ U J_a`, and `rankAux` is a sum of three terms ending in `brigadeM (cannon μ U)`, the `A_μ = A + d_U d_U^* + M_μ` of 7:274 (the first two terms `flare`, `mail` were not read).
*Across chapters:* single occurrence. v3 should restore the definition at 7:276: "let `J_a` select direction `a` from fine links, so `M_μ = Σ_a J_a^* m_μ J_a`".
*See also:* selected.

#### discarded-support
- **Meaning.** Of the error `η` that comes from the supports dropped in a truncation.
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11:1201, 1235. *Proposed:* ordinary words (*the error `η` from the omitted supports*).
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only.

#### discrepancy
*Variants:* discrepancy series; scalar discrepancy; weighted input discrepancies; block average discrepancy; exterior discrepancy.
1. **Discrepancy series:** the family of the `ζ_f`.
   *Basis:* I (9:517). *Where:* 9:517. *Proposed:* name the family (`ζ_f`).
2. **Scalar discrepancy:** the function `f(d) = (β′ + α + d)𝒦(U_*) + …` of the trial shift `d` of the inverse coupling.
   *Basis:* R (9:756–759). *Where:* 9:757. *Proposed:* *the function `f(d)`*.
3. **Difference between the inputs at two parameter values** ("pass to a subsequence whose weighted input discrepancies have sum at most `ε`").
   *Basis:* R (9:791–792). *Where:* 9:791–792; 11:1871 ("discrepancy at most `H^{−v}`"). *Proposed:* *difference*.
4. **Block average discrepancy:** the mismatch `n_e = χ(V_e Q_e(U)⁻¹)` between a coarse link and the block average.
   *Basis:* D (6:47). *Where:* 6:8, 1015, 1342. *Proposed:* *deviation from the block average `n_e`*.
5. **Exterior discrepancy:** a chapter 11 quantity cited by name; not identified.
   *Basis:* ? (17m:426–442). *Where:* 17m:426–442. *Proposed:* cite the equation.
*Across chapters:* five objects under one word.
*See also:* mismatch; trial inverse coupling correction.

#### displacement
*Variants:* displacement `Y`; left link displacement; curvature displacement; displaced coarse current.
- **Meaning.** A vector field `Y` on the product of the link groups (Lie-algebra valued on each link), generating the left variation `U ↦ e^{sY} U`.
  *Basis:* D (17:191–193; 17t:182–186). *Where:* 17:193; 17t:182, 297, 340, 355; 17c:247–291, 312–373; 17m:27, 57 (20 uses). *Proposed:* *vector field* (*infinitesimal left variation*).
*Across chapters:* chapter 17. Not the displacement `x − y` between two points (3:61, 431; 7:146), and not the *displacement field* proposed for the "signal" `ũ` of 6:1373–1383.
*See also:* density identity; separation.

#### distance from the identity
*Variants:* mismatch distance(s) from the identity (4:397); squared group distance (6:1404); squared distance from the identity (4:337).
- **Meaning.** `χ(u) = ‖u − 1‖_F / √n_G`, the normalised Hilbert–Schmidt distance of a group element from the identity, with `χ(u)² = 2w(u)` (1:90–95). The phrase is written out where the symbol would do: "adds a nonnegative squared distance from the identity which is zero at the minimizer" (4:337), "the squared group distance" (6:1404).
  *Basis:* D (1:90–95); 4:56 and 6:49 are reminders (R). *Where:* 1:90–95; 4:56, 337, 397; 6:49, 1014, 1404; 9 + 2 + 13 lines in ch. 4, 5, 6 (14 in ch. 6 with "the squared group distance"). *Proposed:* write `χ(U_p)`, `χ(·)²`; the symbol is defined once, at 1:90.
*Across chapters:* one sense; the definition is in chapter 1 (1:90–95), not at 4:56.
*See also:* mismatch; discrepancy.

#### distant part
- **Meaning.** The complement of the near part in the split of the regular series at connected cover number `M`.
  *Basis:* D (11:1161–1168). *Where:* 11:1161–1169. *Proposed:* keep.
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only.
*See also:* near part.

#### distinguished unit
See *unit* (sense 1).

#### division
*Variants:* elementary division `D_a`; analytic division; homotopy division; (coordinatewise) Taylor division; curl division, division by the lattice curl; coordinate, scalar, two-leg, curvature division.
- **Meaning.** "The elementary division is `D_a f(p) = (f(p) − f(p|_{p_a=0})) / (e^{ip_a} − 1)`" (7:89–91): factoring a difference symbol out of a symbol that vanishes on a coordinate hyperplane; it "loses at most one Taylor order" (7:96–97). Chapter 17 applies it under further names: "Their homotopy divisions lower Taylor order by one each"; "Coordinatewise Taylor division in the remaining eight variables factors two additional differences" (17c:102–105). "Curl-division" (10:314) is the division by the lattice curl of 7:67 ff.
  *Basis:* D (7:89–91); R for the chapter 17 compounds (17c:99–105). *Where:* 7:67, 89–97, 124, 611, 904, 1028, 1105, 1162, 1182; 10:314; 17c:99, 102, 104, 346. *Proposed:* keep, defined once at 7:89; in chapters 10 and 17 refer to Section "Division by the lattice curl".
*Across chapters:* one sense: the chapter 7 definition applies in chapters 10 and 17 (17c:99 cites the chapter 7 section). Not *factorisation of the symbol through difference symbols*: the term is defined and kept.
*See also:* alias; leg.

#### downward blocking
- **Meaning.** The block step from level `m+1` to level `m`.
  *Basis:* R (7:825–856). *Where:* 7:825–856; 9:42 (the list is shared with "one-loop drift"). *Proposed:* *the step from level `m+1` to level `m`*.
*Across chapters:* chapters 7 and 9.
*See also:* one-loop drift; step.

#### dummy Gaussian coordinates
*Variants:* dummy Gaussian integral.
- **Meaning.** Coordinates added to reach a fixed dimension `D`: "let `D` be the dimension after dummy Gaussian coordinates have been added" (9:59); "The dummy Gaussian integral equals one after the inactive Haar variables have been frozen" (9:72–73). Which coordinates are added is not said.
  *Basis:* R (9:59, 72–73). *Where:* 9:59, 72. *Proposed:* *auxiliary Gaussian variables*.
*Across chapters:* chapter 9 only.
*See also:* active coordinates.

### E

#### elementary division
*Variants:* division `D_a`; coordinate, scalar, two-leg, curvature division; curl-division (10:314); "the divisions" (7:1105).
- **Meaning.** The operator `D_a f(p) = (f(p) − f(p|_{p_a=0}))/(e^{ip_a} − 1)` on Taylor symbols, used to divide by the lattice curl; it "loses at most one Taylor order" (7:96–97). The compound forms name the same division applied to a coordinate, a scalar symbol, a two-leg symbol or a curvature symbol.
  *Basis:* D (7:89–91; section "Division by the lattice curl", 7:67). *Where:* 7:67, 89–97, 124, 611, 904, 1028, 1105, 1162, 1182; 10:314–315 ("the linear curl-division and path-placement operations in Chapter 7"); 17c:99, 102. *Proposed:* keep, define once; later chapters cite 7:89–91.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout: "curl-division" (10:314) and the division of chapter 17 are the chapter 7 division (7:67–97).

#### eligible
*Variants:* eligibility; eligibility test; eligibility criteria / conditions / indicators / event; eligibility condition (18:127); eligible family.
1. **Pair satisfying the axial bound.** A pair `(z,o)` is eligible when `Σ_e χ(U_e^{z,o}) ≤ a_ax (2R+1) Σ_□ χ(U_□)`, the sums over links and plaquettes internal to the box.
   *Basis:* D (4:68–75). *Where:* 4:68–75, 224, 252, 314, 361–363. *Proposed:* *pair satisfying the axial bound*.
2. **Additional condition attached to a large-field activity.** A large-field activity has an exclusion support `Y_i`, a nonempty prescribed set `I_i^bad ⊂ Y_i` and "an additional Borel gauge-invariant eligibility test `𝓔_i^extra`"; the activity vanishes outside `{Bad_m(U) ∩ Y_i = I_i^bad} ∩ 𝓔_i^extra`. `𝓔_i^extra` is a set of configurations (an event); the rule defining it is part of the data and is not stated.
   *Basis:* D (4:440–450). *Where:* 4:440–450; 6:83; 8:330; 9:94, 902, 918; 10:669; 11:131, 153, 762, 791; 11R:80, 156, 166–168; 12:25, 181; 13sb:72; 13ba:249; 18:127. *Proposed:* *the additional gauge-invariant condition (event) `𝓔_i^extra` of the activity*.
3. **Allowed covering family.** In the abstract polymer setting the same rule appears as a restriction on families: `𝔆(D)` consists of "the allowed finite families `B` of such labels with disjoint supports and `⋃ I_η = D`. The exact rules for eligibility are part of the definition of an effective density; they may exclude some otherwise possible covers." The sum `Σ_{𝓕 eligible}` of chapter 11 runs over such families.
   *Basis:* R (8:289–295). *Where:* 8:289–295; 11:125. *Proposed:* *allowed covering family*.
*Across chapters:* sense 1 is confined to chapter 4. Senses 2 and 3 are two forms of one rule (per activity in chapter 4, per family in chapter 8). The later uses are sense 2 (text read): 11:131 ("each large-field term retains its original eligibility and large-field conditions"), 11:153 ("original eligibility criteria" of the constituents), 11R:79–80 and 166–168 attach eligibility to terms and labels, so these are sense 2; 11:125 is sense 3.
*See also:* exclusion support; exact cover; event indicator.

#### empty coefficient
*Variants:* empty density.
- **Meaning.** The coefficient of the empty source monomial in the expansion in the nilpotent source variables, that is the density without insertions: "The empty coefficient is exactly one" (11:604); "the empty density, hence its partition function, unchanged" (11:2101). Its integral is the partition function, which chapter 17 calls the denominator.
  *Basis:* R (11:604, 2101). *Where:* 11:604, 773, 2101; 17w:88; 17m:418. *Proposed:* *the density without insertions*.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout; chapter 17 uses it without definition.

#### encoded
- **Meaning.** Expressed in coordinates: "encoded coefficients of a normalized lattice difference".
  *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11:991. *Proposed:* *coefficients of*.
*Across chapters:* one occurrence.

#### encoding weights
See *Hilbert encoding*.

#### endpoint
*Variants:* coarse / bottom endpoint; endpoint estimate; endpoint comparison; endpoint constants; endpoint factors; endpoint re-expression; unit endpoints.
1. **The level-0 coupling.** The value of the inverse coupling at the coarse end of the trajectory ("coarse endpoint").
   *Basis:* R (10:153, 209). *Where:* 10:18, 209, 268–272, 278, 813, 850; 19:21–23. *Proposed:* *value of the coupling at unit scale*.
2. **End of an interval of levels.** The lower or upper end of a plateau or of another interval of levels.
   *Basis:* R (10:139–140). *Where:* 10:139–140, 247. *Proposed:* ordinary usage; keep.
3. **Top level `k` of the restart interval.** The level at which the density is re-expressed with new radius and threshold ("exact endpoint re-expression").
   *Basis:* R (11R:68–70). *Where:* 11:1930, 2092; 11R:68, 89, 384, 387. *Proposed:* *level `k`*.
4. **Last step of a range of steps.** The step at the cutoff `N` (11E:124); "the last-step endpoint estimate" and "the endpoint comparison" (13ba:18, 34) are the estimate at the last level of the interval.
   *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11E:124; 13ba:18, 34. *Proposed:* *estimate at the last step*.
5. **Constants entering a bounded number of times.** "Endpoint constants / factors": constants that enter at the ends of the comparison window and not once per step ("Only a bounded number of endpoint factors is multiplied").
   *Basis:* I (17w:23, 26). *Where:* 17w:23, 26. *Proposed:* *constants entering a bounded number of times*.
6. **End terms of a finite difference or of a telescoping sum.** Ends of a finite difference (11:2287); "unit endpoints" (17m:474), probably the two end terms of a telescoping sum, which are multiples of the identity field.
   *Basis:* R (11:2287); I (17m:474). *Where:* 11:2287; 17m:379–380, 467–475. *Proposed:* *end terms*.
*Across chapters:* the meaning changes with the object that has ends (trajectory, interval, restart window, finite difference). Undetermined: 11:877 "normalized endpoint inequalities"; "endpoint error" (17m:444–470) has no gloss of its own (see *trial descent*). The initial vertex of a link is called its "tail" at 17c:259, not its endpoint.
*See also:* fine end; re-expression of the endpoint.

#### endpoint error
See *trial descent*.

#### endpoint re-expression
See *re-expression of the endpoint*; for the level concerned, *endpoint*, sense 3.

#### energy
*Variants:* selected-component energy; energy reserve.
- **Meaning.** In chapters 10–11, the exponent of the decay factor of a large-field component; the factor itself is its "suppression": "whose suppression is `exp(−cβ_N t_N² n)`" (11:167–168); "selected-component energy" (11R:63); "energy reserve" (11:521).
  *Basis:* R (11:167–168); I for the other two. *Where:* 11:167–168, 521; 11R:63. *Proposed:* *exponent of the decay factor*.
*Across chapters:* this entry covers only the chapter 10–11 use. Other compounds are treated elsewhere: "heat energy" (14:414) is the spectral variable of `H` (see *heat*); plaquette, local and core energy are separate terms.

#### entry
*Variants:* lower / higher entry; higher (regular) entries; regular entry linear in the sources (13ba:163).
1. **Member of a family.** A member `P_i` of the family.
   *Basis:* I. *Where:* 11R:384–385. *Proposed:* *member*.
2. **Term of the local representation of the marked density**, of any source degree: "this adds `F_v` only to the regular entry linear in the sources" (13ba:162–163). The "higher (regular) entries" are the terms containing at least two source variables `z_i` ("Every term in `H_X` and `K_Q^{≥2}` contains at least two distinct source variables … set only these higher entries to zero", 12:207–209; "Multiply every term of source degree at least two, and only those entries, by a complex scalar `u`", 12:270–271). The degree is carried by "higher", not by "entry".
   *Basis:* R (12:200–209, 270–271; 13ba:162–163). *Where:* 12:202, 209, 271; 13ba:163. *Proposed:* *term*; *terms of source degree ≥ 2* for the higher entries (the text has "source degree" at 12:270).
*Across chapters:* two unrelated uses: sense 1 in 11R, sense 2 in chapters 12 and 13ba.

#### envelope
*Variants:* summable envelope; output envelope; weighted output envelope; scalar envelope; polynomial envelope; derivative envelopes.
- **Meaning.** A majorant that dominates a whole family at once: "Their sum added to the majorant at `u_0` is a common summable envelope" (9:793–794); the display 11:1580–1582 (`exp{unmarked exponent + q_0(1+n)}`, label `ch11:weighted-output-envelope`); "`p(z) ≥ 1` is a polynomial envelope for the finite Gaussian coordinates" (17m:283).
  *Basis:* R (9:793–794; 17m:283); I at 6:1187. *Where:* 6:1187; 9:159, 690, 793–796; 11:1972, 2136 (display 11:1580–1582); 17m:283. *Proposed:* *majorant* (*common majorant* where it bounds a family).
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout. At 6:1187 ("exponentially small weighted entry and fixed derivative envelopes for `D`") the same reading fits (inferred; text read). Not interchangeable with the text's own "majorant", which bounds a single factor or activity (9:106, 124, 655), whereas the envelope of 9:793–794 is built from majorants.

#### equation calibration floor
*Variants:* calibration floor (label `ch11:calibration-floor`).
- **Meaning.** The lower bound `L^{1/8} ≥ max_{d≤j} 2(1+C_j) Q_{dj} δ_d^{-1}` on the block ratio `L` (label `ch11:calibration-floor`), where `Q_{dj} = 2 + e^{81σ_j}(a_{dj} + C_j + 2q_d)` and `δ_d = (2𝒪_d²)^{-1}` (11E:15–23). The text includes it "in the stage-`j` block floor" (11E:23–29): the block floor is the whole collection of lower bounds on the block ratio at stage `j`, and this bound is one member of it. The same sentence adds a separate condition on the coupling, `β̂_N ≥ a_{d,J(N)}`, "in the adjacent stage conditions on the starting scale"; this second condition is not called a floor. 19:29–31 ("finite stage requirements, such as the equation calibration floor") may be meant to cover both.
  *Basis:* R (11E:15–30). *Where:* 11E:23–30; 19:30. *Proposed:* *the lower bound (11.calibration-floor) on the block ratio `L`*, with the accompanying condition on `β̂_N`.
  *Source:* Martin `existence/marked-portfolio-calibration.tex:186–221`: "The sphere bound is `S_i(q_d,a) = 2 + e^{81α_i}(a + c_i + 2q_d)` … [the] sliver `δ_d = 1/(2𝒪_d²)` … Since the volume purse is `P(L) = L^{1/8} → ∞`, choose an integer `n_{di}` such that `2(1+c_i) S_i(q_d,a_{di}) ≤ P(L) δ_d` (`L ≥ n_{di}`)"; the threshold of stage `i` is the maximum of the `n_{di}`, `d ≤ i`, and of the `v_j`, `j ≤ i`, where `(1+2c_j) L^{−2/5} ≤ L^{−3/8}` for `L ≥ v_j`. Lean `YM.MergeProof.sphere` (`YM/MergeProof/Matter.lean:34`; definition read) `= 2 + exp(81·supportExponent)·(b + columns + 2p)`; `YM.MergeProof.sliver` (`YM/MergeProof/Marimba.lean:18`; definition read) `= (2·orbitCost²)⁻¹`; `YM.Bid.puffs` (`YM/Bid/Loan.lean:34`; definition read) `= L^{1/8}`; `YM.PhysicalNext.Repeat.Legato.paper` and `oyster` (`YM/MergeProof/Apres.lean:20–21`; definition and statement read): thresholds `l i` exist such that for all `d ≤ i` and `L ≥ l i`, `2(1+columns_i)·sphere ≤ puffs L · sliver`, together with a credit clause and `(1+2·columns_j)·rate L ≤ barunit L` for `j ≤ i` (`Bid.Credit` and `Doors.rate` were not opened).
*Across chapters:* one sense; used in chapter 19, stated in 11E (text read at 11E:13–31). In the sources the same threshold also contains the inequality `(1+2C_j) L^{−2/5} ≤ L^{−3/8}`, which v3 uses at 18lp:41–42 ("The block floor makes this at most `L_l^{−3/8} q`") without a reference; v3 should state it with (11.calibration-floor).
*See also:* floor (sense 1); block floor.

#### equation direction
*Variants:* `v_i^eq`; `v_eom`.
- **Meaning.** The vector `v_i^eq = β_i^{-1}Σ_{k_i} − j_i` given by the formula at 17m:386, which converges to `v_eom`. `v_eom = (0,0,1) ∈ E = ℝ³` is the kernel vector `v` of the free quotient map `s : E → V` (17:171–172); the third coordinate of `E` is the Maxwell-equation term `Σ⟨F_bc, ∂_a F_ac⟩` (17:169), "the Maxwell equation direction". 17m:383 refers to "the notation of the stability argument", where 17:262–264 has "one-dimensional kernel `ℝv`" and "`v_i → v`". `v_i^eq` is a different object from `v_eom`: it is the approximating sequence.
  *Basis:* D for `v_i^eq` (17m:386); S for `v_eom` (the v3 text does not introduce it; 17:171–172 gives the same vector under the name `v`). *Where:* 17m:375 (subsection title), 385–386. *Proposed:* *kernel vector `v` of `s`*; write `v` for `v_eom`.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:133` "It annihilates the third coordinate, the Maxwell equation direction. … The free Maxwell quotient map `s : R_5 → V_5` is onto, with `ker s = ℝ v_eom`, `v_eom = (0,0,1)` and `ρ_tr(v_eom) = 0`"; `I-section.tex:390–391`, the display reproduced at 17m:385–386.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only.
*See also:* `v_eom`.

#### equation ideal
*Variants:* `𝓘_d`; free equation ideal (2:445).
- **Meaning.** The ideal `𝓘_d` of polynomials that vanish on jets of solutions of the free (Maxwell) equations.
  *Basis:* D (2e:10–21). *Where:* 2e:10–21; 2:445. *Proposed:* keep, define once.
*Across chapters:* one sense; it is the ideal whose image at cutoff `(N,p)` is the *equation space*.

#### equation remainder
- **Meaning.** The normalised difference `(x_u − Π_u x_u)/(1 + ‖Π_u x_u‖)` of the argument of 13:195–203, which 18gq:108–110 applies again; "Their difference lies in the exact finite equation kernel" (13:220).
  *Basis:* R (13:195–203, 220). *Where:* 18gq:110. *Proposed:* none proposed; write the expression, citing 13:195–203.
*Across chapters:* used in 18gq, determined by chapter 13.
*See also:* equation space.

#### equation space
*Variants:* equation subspace / kernel / labels / component; finite equation kernel; moving, varying, actual equation space; microscopic equation space; equation comparison; equation inclusion.
- **Meaning.** The image at cutoff `(N,p)` of the equation ideal: `𝖤_{N,p,d} = 𝖹 P S_{t_N} R_d 𝓘_d` (11E:155–159), written `K_i = X_i P S_t R_e I_e` at 11:1089–1093; in chapter 13 it is `ker Π_{d,N,p}`, given by the same formula without a symbol (13:136–137). "Moving", "varying" and "actual" say that it depends on `(N,p)`. "Equation labels" are the elements of `I^𝒱_{N,d} = S_{t_N} R_d 𝓘_d` (11E:43–46), a space independent of `p`, whose image under `𝖹_{N,p,d} P_{N,p,d}` is the equation subspace "in reference coordinates" (11E:154–159). "Equation comparison" compares the two realisations of the equations of motion.
  *Basis:* D (11E:155–159; 11:1089–1093). *Where:* 11:966, 989, 1083, 1089–1093, 1107, 2218, 2224; 11E:43–46, 154–159; 13:14, 15–16, 136–137, 157, 220, 394; 18gq:10, 110. *Proposed:* *space of equation-of-motion labels at cutoff `(N,p)`*.
*Across chapters:* one object: `𝖤_{N,p,d}` in 11E, `K_i` in chapter 11 (11:1089–1093, 2218), `E_i` in the abstract lemma (11:965–967), and the formula without a symbol in chapter 13 (13:136–137). Not *cutoff-dependent subspace of field equations*: the elements are images of labels; the cutoff dependence is stated in the proposed name instead.
*See also:* equation ideal; equation remainder.

#### `E_stat`, `E_tail`, `E_mark`
*Variants:* `E_reg` as an error coefficient (17m:161).
- **Meaning.** The four error coefficients of (17.finite-sigma), `Σ_k = 𝒫_{5,t}(div_Haar Y − D𝓛[Y]) + E_stat + E_tail + E_reg + E_mark` (17m:158–162). `E_stat` is the change in the degree-five coefficient caused by truncating the stationary kernels at radius `C_j(log β̂_k)²`; `E_tail` is the same for the loop paths of `𝓛` longer than that radius ("Here stationary and loop kernels are truncated at `C_j(log β̂_k)²`. Their common exponential decay makes `E_stat` and `E_tail` at most `H^{-1}`", 17m:163–165). `E_mark` is "the marked remainder" (17m:176): what the marked step leaves after the radial Taylor coefficients through degree five are cancelled on nonwrapping supports, together with the large-field and wrapping contributions; it is bounded in (17.sigma-error) (17m:325). The fourth error, written `E_reg` at 17m:161, is the classical defect: the degree-five coefficient contributed by the regular term `E_reg` of `Z_ord = 𝒞 exp[−βS − 𝓛 − E_reg]` (17m:107), bounded by `t^{-2} ε_k^reg = β̂_k^{-1/10} H^{-2}` (17m:166–169). By 17m:104–111 and 168–171 ("A directional derivative along `Y` has the same bound") it is the extracted coefficient `𝒫_{5,t}(−D E_reg[Y])` of the directional derivative of the regular term.
  *Basis:* R (17m:163–169, 176) for the bounds; S for what each error is; I for the identification of the fourth error with `𝒫_{5,t}(−D E_reg[Y])`. *Where:* 17m:161–176; (17.sigma-error) 17m:325. *Proposed:* define each in a sentence after (17.finite-sigma); rename the fourth error, for example `E_cl := 𝒫_{5,t}(−D E_reg[Y])`, so that `E_reg` names only the regular term of 17m:107.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/I-section.tex:358–362` (I-five-pieces) "`… + ε_stat + ε_tail + ε_cl + ε_mark` … The errors are stationary substitution, omitted loop paths, the classical defect and the marked remainder. Each has norm at most `e^{-h_k}`: truncate stationary kernels and loop paths at `C_j(log β̂_k)²` … The activity caps … bound `ε_cl` in the seminorm of Definition D05a"; `I-section.tex:366` "For `ε_mark`, Lemma E2.2a cancels the radial Taylor coefficients through degree five on nonwrapping supports". Scott names and bounds `ε_cl` and does not write it as a derivative of the regular term.
*Across chapters:* 17m only. One letter `E_reg` is used for the function at 17m:107 and for the coefficient of its derivative along `Y` at 17m:161. `E_tail` is not a Gaussian tail (see *tail*): it is the contribution of the omitted loop paths. v3 should restore, after (17.finite-sigma), the sentence of Scott I:362: "The errors are stationary substitution, omitted loop paths, the classical defect and the marked remainder."
*See also:* regular (sense 1); tail; mark; stationary substitution.

#### event indicator
*Variants:* event indicators; fixed Borel event indicator; health event indicator.
- **Meaning.** The indicator function of a Borel event of the configuration (small-field, large-field or cutoff condition) attached to a term; it is not smooth and is not differentiated: "its event indicator may read additional adjacent plaquettes" (4:507); "fixed Borel event indicator … no continuity of the event indicator as a function of `U` is required" (12:163–164).
  *Basis:* R (4:507; 12:163–164). *Where:* 4:507, 532, 658; ch. 6 (8 uses); 9:19, 283, 348, 408, 494, 500, 545, 571, 575, 837, 839; ch. 10 (11 uses); ch. 11 (8); 11R (9); 12:25, 163–164. *Proposed:* *indicator of the event*; say which event.
*Across chapters:* one sense, the word alternating with "test" in chapters 4 and 6 and replacing it from chapter 10 on. In chapter 9 not every use is the small-field indicator `h_X` (9:19 is generic; 9:283 and 9:837 are not tied to `h_X`), so the phrase is not a synonym of *small-field indicator*.
*See also:* event label; health; eligible.

#### event label
*Variants:* cutoff-failure label (9:111, 133).
- **Meaning.** The index `w` of a cutoff remainder: it "specifies one particular cutoff and its anchor"; a remainder with event label `w` vanishes unless the event `ℰ_w` occurs, on which that cutoff fails (the text's "large-coordinate event").
  *Basis:* D (6:835–843). *Where:* 6:835–877, 1106; 9:111, 133. *Proposed:* *event label*, one name; the event `ℰ_w` is the *cutoff-failure event* (never "large-field event").
*Across chapters:* one sense; chapter 9 renames it. Chapters 10–16 do not use it and speak of event indicators instead, which are a different object (functions, not indices).
*See also:* event indicator.

#### exact
*Variants:* exact blocking; exact block map; exact (normalised) block kernel.
- **Meaning.** Said of the block kernel: it is a probability kernel, so that the partition function is preserved by the block step.
  *Basis:* D (4:289). *Where:* 4:2, 5, 169, 232, 289, 569; 1:440; 9:49. *Proposed:* *normalised block-spin kernel*.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout.

#### exact cover
*Variants:* exact coverage; exact large-field indicator coverage.
- **Meaning.** A family of large-field activities with pairwise disjoint exclusion supports `Y_i` whose prescribed large-field sets have union `Bad_m(U)`; in chapter 8, `⋃ I_η = D`.
  *Basis:* D (4:543–547). *Where:* 4:543–547; 8:289–292, 336–347; 9:82–95, 407, 634–641, 890; 11:134–136, 150, 180, 246–251; 11R:8, 124, 157, 167–168; 12:180, 188. *Proposed:* *compatible family covering the large-field set*.
*Across chapters:* one sense throughout.
*See also:* eligible; exclusion support; exact-cover gas.

#### exact-cover gas
- **Meaning.** The large-field factor of the density: `𝒢(U) = Σ_b ∏_{i∈b} K_i(U)`, the sum over finite families `b` of large-field activities with pairwise disjoint supports whose prescribed large-field sets have union exactly the set of large-field sites of `U`; it equals 1 when `U` has no large-field site. The text calls it "a finite polynomial in the latter profiles and fixed eligibility indicators" (12:180–182). It is a function of the configuration and only one factor of the density: `ρ̃ = e^{-s}ρ` is its product with the exponential of the regular action, and `Z⁰ = ∫ρ̃ dμ` (12:172–183). In chapter 9 the same phrase names `ℱ⁰` (9:593).
  *Basis:* R (12:180–183); S for the summation condition and the value 1. *Where:* 9:593; 12:180. *Proposed:* *large-field polymer sum over exact covers*, or keep, define once.
  *Source:* Lean `YM.RG.Activities.gas`, YM/RG/Activities.lean (definition read: `gas U = Σ' b : Finset ℕ, gasOccurrence b U`, with `gasOccurrence b U = ∏_{i∈b} K_i(U)` if `admissible U b`, else 0); `Activities.admissible`, same file (definition read; docstring "Disjoint, exact coverage": supports of the members of `b` pairwise disjoint and `⋃_{i∈b} inventory_i = flags p.threshold U`); `YM.RG.flags`, YM/RG/Masks.lean (definition read: the sites touching a plaquette whose chord exceeds the threshold); `Activities.gas_one` (statement read: the gas is 1 if no site is flagged); `YM.RG.Rep.eval`, YM/RG/History.lean (definition read: `eval U = exp(exponent U) · gas U`, `exponent = v·|sites| − path action − sum of regular activities`). Martin existence/fixed-rung-convergence.tex:221–233: "Its gas is a finite sum over compatible subsets of these profiles, each multiplied by the fixed flag indicator … [the scalar-stripped density] is the product of the gas and the exponential of minus the path action and ordinary activity sum".
*Across chapters:* one sense. In chapter 9 the identification with `ℱ⁰` is inferred. "Unmarked gas" (18lp:186, once) is the same factor for the density without source variables (see *unmarked gas*). Not *partition function* and not *density without insertions*: the gas is one factor of the density (12:172–183). Not *constrained sum `ℱ⁰`* as the book-wide name: it names the chapter 9 symbol only.
*See also:* gas; exact cover; unmarked gas.

#### exact pulled-back defect
*Variants:* stationary pullback; stationary substitution `𝓘`.
- **Meaning.** The current defect composed with the stationary fine field: `𝓘F = F(U_stat(V))`.
  *Basis:* D (17t:28). *Where:* 17t:157, 159; for the substitution `𝓘` also 17t:28; 17c:51, 72, 77, 91, 208, 304. *Proposed:* *composition with the stationary field*, applied to the current defect.
*Across chapters:* chapter 17 only.
*See also:* stationary substitution.

#### exact reassembly
- **Meaning.** The factorisation identity `Z_D = e^{𝓛} Σ_B Π K_η e^{−𝓛_{Y(B)}}` of the polymer expansion.
  *Basis:* R (8:310–316). *Where:* 8:279, 355; 9:57. *Proposed:* *factorisation identity*.
*Across chapters:* one sense. The related identity of Proposition 9:651 ("exact regrouping", label "fusion") is a different statement; see *fusion*.

#### exact unit rule
- **Meaning.** The fact that each step sends the identity field `e_0` exactly to `L^d e_0`, with zero remainder: "The unit has zero remainders and is sent exactly to `L^d` times itself" (11:451). It gives the reference coefficient `a_{r(d)}^d e_0` of the identity field in a degree-`d` convention (11:87–90; "the exact unit rule gives the reference unit coefficient `a_{r(d)}^d e_0`", 11:1049–1050). A compound of *unit*, sense 1.
  *Basis:* R (11:451, 1049–1050). *Where:* 11:1049–1050 (one occurrence). *Proposed:* *the rule for the identity field `e_0`*, stated once (`e_0 ↦ L^d e_0`).
*Across chapters:* chapter 11 only; "unit" is rendered *identity field* throughout.
*See also:* unit.

#### exceptional phases
*Variants:* the exceptional set; exceptional vacua (19:107).
- **Meaning.** The `ν`-null set of phases outside which `ker H_ξ = ℂΩ_ξ` is proved (15:320–326: "we have not eliminated exceptional phases"). The text never shows that uniqueness fails there; it is later obtained for every phase (16:379–381: "the zero-energy space is a line for almost every phase … To remove the exceptional set requires a bound uniform in `ξ`"). "Exceptional vacua" (19:107, once) refers to this set, not to a kind of vector: "remove exceptional vacua" means "prove `ker H_ξ = ℂΩ_ξ` for every phase `ξ`, not only for `ν`-almost every one".
  *Basis:* R (15:320–326; 16:379–381). *Where:* 15:325, 328, 339; 16:380; 19:107. *Proposed:* *the null set of phases on which uniqueness of the vacuum is not yet known*; for 19:105–107, *… extend uniqueness of the vacuum from almost every phase to every phase*.
  *Source:* Scott `part2/H-section.tex:211`: "Vacuum uniqueness first holds only for `ν`-almost every phase (Lemma `lem:H1.3`). The low-energy estimate of Lemma `lem:H2.3` is uniform in the phase; with the continuity in `ξ` of the vacuum-subtracted heat pairings and the full support of `ν`, it removes the exceptional set." Lean not searched.
*Across chapters:* one sense. Not *non-uniqueness of the vacuum on the `ν`-null set of phases*: the text does not show that uniqueness fails there (text read at 15:324–328, 16:379–381, 19:105–108). Not *further invariant vectors*, for the same reason.

#### exceptional vacua
See *exceptional phases*.

3. **The `ε` above the sum of degrees.** In the sharp bounds, the arbitrarily small loss in the exponent ("the loss … can be reduced to an arbitrarily small excess").

*Across chapters:* three uses. Senses 1 and 3 are not slack in an estimate (6:326–329; 13sb:6–7): sense 1 is a contribution that is not small, sense 3 a loss. The word is therefore not a synonym of *reserve* or of the "strict margin" of 18lp:257 and 16:201, which are slack.
